answer: Filling 39 aliases thus means producing 39 separate sets of claims, which is authoring work rather than a lookup. Because the harbor count is verified against the kernel text itself, the vine audit records each rejection and the operator cannot amortise one paragraph. An answer claiming a deep mechanism must supply at least 3 distinct supporting claims, and the count is checked before grading so shallow text cannot pass by padding. That is 29 dollars per alias. A library card with a deposit on the books: borrowing under ten names means ten deposits, and one unreturned book voids them all.
